Jonas — reviewed. High level summary below; see attached PDF for inline comments and rationale.

Key positions:
- Data residency: We can accept carve-outs for specific EU-to-US transfer clauses but will require SCCs if personal data for EU residents is involved. Suggest proposed language: "Redwood will store customer content in customer-selected regions where available; for EU personal data, SCCs will be appended."
- Subprocessors: We accept the limited subprocessor list but push back on open-ended "may engage" language. Recommend a defined subprocessors clause with 30-day notice and the right to object for high-risk subprocessors.
- Incident notification: We confirm 72-hour notification for incidents affecting personal data; for critical incidents we will notify within 24 hours.

Attachments: Redline_comments_summary.pdf (summary of changes and recommended counter), DPA_Redline_v1_with_legal_comments.docx

If FinCore insists on blanket residency guarantees, that will need exec sign-off and could affect pricing. Jonas — can you flag the prospect of a residency carveout exception, and if necessary I'll escalate to Ops/Privacy.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
